ADDM Task ADDM:659179364_1_14174

          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:659179364_1_14174'
          ---------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 14173 to 14174.
Time period starts at 02-DEC-25 11.30.37 AM
Time period ends at 02-DEC-25 12.31.01 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'KRISHNA' with DB ID 659179364.
Database version during analysis period was 19.25.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance krishna, numbered 1 and hosted at
kirshnadb-pr.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 17823 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 4.92.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect   1.27 | 25.89         1
2  Soft Parse                       .92 | 18.77          2
3  Top SQL Statements               .4 | 8.21            2
4  Unusual "Other" Wait Event       .3 | 6.11            3
5  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations  .27 | 5.59           1
6  Undersized SGA                   .11 | 2.28           1
7  Java Execution                   .11 | 2.21           1
8  Unusual "Other" Wait Event       .11 | 2.18           3


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.27 active sessions, 25.89% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.27 active sessions, 25.89% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is .92 active sessions, 18.77% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .92 active sessions, 18.77% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .92 active sessions, 18.77% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .4 active sessions, 8.21% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .27 active sessions, 5.41% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 5% for SQL execution,
      26% for parsing, 69% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .14 active sessions, 2.8% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "02uwhh1490jct" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 02uwhh1490jct.
         BEGIN PKG_CBVER02_FRDRTGSFL.READ_FILES_PARTICULAR(:1,:2,:3,:4,:5);
         END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 3% for SQL execution,
      2% for parsing, 23% for PL/SQL execution and 72% for Java execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "02uwhh1490jct" was executed 12741 times and
      had an average elapsed time of 0.044 seconds.
   Rationale
      Waiting for event "OJVM: Generic" in wait class "Other" accounted for
      72% of the database time spent in processing the SQL statement with
      SQL_ID "02uwhh1490jct".


Finding 4: Unusual "Other" Wait Event
Impact is .3 active sessions, 6.11% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "Failed Logon Delay" in wait class "Other" was consuming
significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .3 active sessions, 6.11% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits. Refer to
      Oracle's "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

   Recommendation 2: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .3 active sessions, 6.11% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits in Module
      "oracle@kirshnadb-pr".

   Recommendation 3: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .3 active sessions, 6.11% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits in Service
      "SYS$USERS".

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Other" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .42 active sessions, 8.6% of total activity.


Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .27 active sessions, 5.59% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .27 active sessions, 5.59% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.
